previous_disclosures.section: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements > European Matters > Tax
previous_disclosures.summary: The Dutch Tax Authority is challenging in Dutch courts the prior set-off taken by the Firm in cases numbered 15/3637 and 15/4353.

The Dutch Authority alleged the Firm was not entitled to approximately €124 million in withholding tax credits for tax years 2007-2012, claiming the subsidiary lacked legal title to securities and failed to provide adequate information and records. In January 2024, the Dutch High Court granted the Firm's appeal and referred the case to the Court of Appeal in The Hague.

In June 2021, Dutch criminal authorities began investigating the Firm regarding the accuracy of tax returns and maintenance of books and records for 2007-2012, which is ongoing as the Firm continues to respond to requests for additional information.

comparisons.peer_summary: A Dutch foundation filed claims in 2021 for institutional investor losses related to FX manipulation; after partial dismissal in 2023, the claimant appealed and filed new writs in September 2023 and January 2025 to assert similar claims on behalf of additional investors.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and C disclose specific, ongoing legal proceedings in the Netherlands involving complex financial allegations. MS describes a resolved civil tax dispute (€124M withholding tax credits) that was settled in November 2024, while an associated criminal investigation remains ongoing. In contrast, C discloses an active, multi-year civil litigation filed in 2021 regarding FX manipulation, which involved partial dismissals and subsequent appeals, with no settlement indicated for the 2024 period. While both involve Dutch jurisdiction and significant legal risk, MS's civil component concluded via settlement in 2024, whereas C's remains in the appeals phase.

sentences.text: On November 11, 2024, the Firm reached an agreement to settle the Dutch Authority's challenges for the tax years 2007 to 2012 and made payment of the prior set-off amounts and interest indicated above.

The Dutch criminal authorities have requested additional information, and the Firm is continuing to respond to them in connection with their ongoing investigation, and is engaging with them as the criminal process progresses.
In March 2023, the court dismissed claims made on behalf of parties located outside the Netherlands and permitted the other claims to go forward.
Claimant appealed that decision and in September 2023 and January 2025 filed new writs of summons asserting similar claims on behalf of additional institutional investors.

comparisons.peer_summary: The firm participates in the IRS CAP program for tax years 2013-2025; issues for 2011-2018 are resolved pending Joint Committee review, and 2019-2022 are resolved pending IRS administrative completion, with no material impact on the effective tax rate expected for those years.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and GS disclose the status of specific tax-related regulatory matters, but the nature and outcome of the proceedings differ fundamentally. MS details a contentious civil challenge by the Dutch Tax Authority over historical tax credits (2007-2012) which was settled in November 2024, accompanied by a separate ongoing criminal investigation. GS, conversely, describes its participation in the IRS Compliance Assurance Process (CAP), a collaborative pre-filing review mechanism. GS reports that issues for recent tax years (2011-2022) have been 'resolved' through this cooperative process, resulting in no material impact on the effective tax rate. Unlike MS's adversarial settlement and ongoing criminal probe, GS's disclosure reflects routine, cooperative resolution of federal tax issues.
